paper_a.title: On the Brunn-Minkowski inequality for general measures with applications to new isoperimetric-type inequalities

paper_b.title: Harmonic Interpolation and a Brunn-Minkowski Theorem for Random Determinants

metadata.description: Both papers prove Brunn-Minkowski-type inequalities, but in disjoint formulations and with very different machinery. Paper A extends classical BM from Lebesgue measure to broader classes of measures (unconditional product, 2D even log-concave) via a refined unconditional Prekopa-Leindler inequality. Paper B keeps the Lebesgue volume but generalises the Minkowski sum to a harmonic interpolation of convex bodies parametrised by a domain, proving superharmonicity of the volume root using subharmonic-family methods drawn from complex analysis (Berndtsson/Kiselman). The shared concepts are the classical Brunn-Minkowski inequality and the support function; the contributions and proof techniques are otherwise non-overlapping.

matches.explanation: Both nodes state the classical Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Lebesgue volume, $|\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B|^{1/n} \geq \lambda |A|^{1/n} + (1-\lambda)|B|^{1/n}$ (paper B writes it in the equivalent additive form $|A+B|^{1/n} \geq |A|^{1/n} + |B|^{1/n}$). Paper A lists it as the cited classical equation that motivates the generalisation; paper B cites it as the engine driving the harmonic-interpolation proof. Both are tagged origin: external.

Both definitions invoke the support function $h_A(\xi) = \sup_{x \in A} \langle x, \xi\rangle$ of a convex set. Paper A only uses the support function to define the symmetric geometric mean $\odot^S$ (a multiplicative-in-support-function operation on symmetric convex sets); paper B uses it as a stand-alone classical tool to encode set inclusions and to recast subharmonicity. Conceptually identical object playing different supporting roles in the two theories.

Paper A's definition abstracts the Brunn-Minkowski inequality as a property a measure $\mu$ may or may not satisfy on a class $\mathcal{K}$; paper B's TP461.1 is the concrete classical instance ($\mu = $ Lebesgue, $\mathcal{K}=$ all convex bodies). The A-side definition strictly generalises the B-side statement, but B never abstracts the property, so the match is one-directional and analogous.
Paper A's main Theorem 1 (BM in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for unconditional product measures with decreasing density on the class of ideals) has no counterpart in paper B, which never leaves Lebesgue volume.
Paper A's two-dimensional Theorem 2 for symmetric convex sets and even log-concave measures, which resolves the 2D Gardner-Zvavitch case, is paper-A-specific.
Theorem 4 (BM for unconditional log-concave measures on ideals) is again a measure-generalisation result that has no counterpart in paper B.
The unconditional Prekopa-Leindler with parameter $p$ (Proposition 1) is the central new functional inequality of paper A; paper B uses no Prekopa-Leindler-type tool.
Proposition 2 (log-BM with radially decreasing density implies BM) is a paper-A-specific technical step; paper B never works with log-BM.
Lemma 1 (parametric set-form of the unconditional Prekopa-Leindler) is paper-A internal.
The 1D unconditional BM lemma is paper-A internal; paper B has no 1D reduction.
Concavity of parallel volume $t \mapsto \mu(A+tB)^{1/n}$ for nice pairs is a paper-A application drawn from its measure-generalised BM.
Brunn-type theorem for $\mu$-sections is a paper-A specific corollary.
Mixed Gaussian isoperimetric / reverse-S inequality is unique to paper A.
Minkowski-first-type inequality for nice pairs is unique to paper A.
Unconditional function: paper-A specific structural definition with no counterpart in paper B.
Decreasing unconditional function: paper-A specific.
Ideal class $\mathcal{K}_I$: paper-A specific class of sets.
Symmetric convex sets $\mathcal{K}_S$: while paper B works with convex bodies, it never restricts to the symmetric class; this definition is paper-A specific in usage.
Unconditional measure: paper-A specific.
Geometric mean of sets: paper-A axiomatisation that supports the log-BM formulation; absent in paper B.
Log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality for a measure: paper-A specific multiplicative variant.
Ideal geometric mean $\odot^I$: paper-A specific construction.
$s$-concave measure: paper-A specific.
Log-concave measure: paper-A specific definition; paper B does not classify measures by log-concavity.
Nice pair $(\mathcal{K}, \mu)$: paper-A specific umbrella definition for the BM measure-class theorems.
First mixed volume $V_1^\mu(A,B)$: paper-A specific functional used in the Minkowski-first corollary.
$\mu$-surface area: paper-A specific.
Functional $M_\mu(A)$: paper-A specific.
Optimal $p$ choice in the parametric Prekopa-Leindler argument: paper-A internal.
Differential identity for $M_\mu$: paper-A internal.
Open problem on BM for symmetric sets and even log-concave measures: paper-A specific.
Proof of Theorem 1 from Lemma 1 is paper-A internal; no analogue in paper B.
Proof of Lemma 1 from Proposition 1 is paper-A internal.
Inductive proof of Proposition 1 is paper-A internal.
Proof of Proposition 2 is paper-A internal.
Proof of Theorem 3 via Prekopa-Leindler is paper-A internal.
Proof of Corollary 1 is paper-A internal.
Proof of Corollary 2 is paper-A internal.
Proof of Corollary 4 is paper-A internal.
Proof of Lemma 2 (1D unconditional BM) is paper-A internal.
Convex interpolation is a paper-B-specific construction (the discrete-boundary cousin of harmonic interpolation); paper A has no analogous boundary-parametrised interpolation.
Minkowski integral (set-valued integration via support functions) is paper-B-specific; paper A only uses ordinary Minkowski sums.
Harmonic interpolation of a boundary family of convex bodies via harmonic measure is the central new construction of paper B; paper A has no continuous interpolation parameter.
Subharmonic family of convex sets is a paper-B-specific notion.
Paper B's main theorem: superharmonicity of $|A_x|^{1/n}$ for harmonic interpolation. The harmonic-interpolation framing is absent from paper A.
Subharmonic-family corollary is paper-B-specific.
Strengthened Berndtsson theorem (volume-root version of plurisubharmonicity of $-\log|U_w|$) is paper-B-specific and lives in complex analysis.

Characterisation of the harmonic / extremal case for harmonic interpolation is paper-B-specific. Paper A's Remark 2 on equality cases concerns its own Theorems 2 and 4 with a completely different statement (dilation in BM equality).
Brunn-Minkowski for expected absolute random determinants (the headline application of paper B) has no counterpart in paper A.
Proof of TP461.3 by atomic-measure approximation plus classical BM is paper-B internal.
Proof of strengthened Berndtsson theorem via Kiselman's minimum principle is paper-B internal.
Proof of extremal characterisation is paper-B internal.
Proof of TP461.8 via zonoids and the Vitale identity is paper-B internal.
